title: Abéché march against appointment of a Bani Halba traditional canton chief
location: Abéché, Ouaddaï province; route from Mahamat Yacoub Dobio high school to Independence Square
participants_original: Human Rights Watch and CTDDH: “thousands of peaceful protesters.”
threshold_50_evidence: A joint HRW–CTDDH investigation explicitly reports thousands of protesters marching in Abéché, which is well above 50; no numeric bounds are derived from this qualitative wording.

start_date.summary: HRW/CTDDH date the street march to January 24.

end_date.summary: HRW/CTDDH report that security forces dispersed the march with tear gas and live fire on Jan 24; the Jan 25 funeral is a separate gathering.

location.summary: HRW/CTDDH give the march route from Mahamat Yacoub Dobio high school to Independence Square in Abéché.

scope.summary: The protest took place in Abéché, Ouaddaï province.

organizer.summary: The report identifies the crowd and demand but does not identify a march organizer.

demands.summary: Demonstrators opposed plans to appoint a Bani Halba traditional chief in a city already represented by an Ouaddaïen sultan.

participants_original.summary: HRW/CTDDH describe thousands of peaceful protesters.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The explicitly reported “thousands” is a qualitative threshold comfortably above 50; no lower or upper numeric bound inferred.

protester_violence.summary: The march is described as peaceful; the article reports a commander’s later claim about weapons found but does not report protesters using them or committing violence.

state_response.arrests.summary: Security forces arrested 212 people during the January 24 protests; releases occurred Jan 25–28.

state_response.beatings.summary: The report says security forces beat some of those arrested during the Jan 24 protest response.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Security forces violently dispersed the peaceful march using tear gas and live fire.

state_response.killings.summary: HRW/CTDDH report three protesters killed by security forces on January 24.

state_response.shootings.summary: HRW/CTDDH report soldiers fired live rounds at the march.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No accommodation of the march demand is established in the contemporaneous response account; later leader replacement is dated Feb 23 and its reason is unspecified.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not establish that authorities ignored the protest.

notes: Local political/customary appointment dispute. Keep separate from the Jan 25 burial gathering; do not merge the march and funeral on the basis of temporal linkage. A minister denied that security forces used live ammunition, while HRW/CTDDH and witnesses report otherwise.
open_questions: Who organized the march?
Was the appointment formally issued or only planned at the time of the march?
Review local customary leadership target against the verified original codebook before approval.

title: Abéché funeral gathering for people killed during the January 24 protest
location: Tago Zagalo cemetery area, Abéché, Ouaddaï province
participants_original: HRW/CTDDH: thousands of people attended the burial of those killed the previous day; a witness said participants held signs saying they were coming in peace.
threshold_50_evidence: HRW/CTDDH report thousands attending the burial, well above 50; no numeric bounds are derived. Whether this funeral gathering was a protest action remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: The funeral gathering and firing are dated January 25.

end_date.summary: The source dates the burial gathering and shooting to Jan 25 but does not establish when the gathering physically ended.

location.summary: HRW/CTDDH place the burial and firing at Tago Zagalo cemetery in Abéché.

scope.summary: The gathering was a local funeral in Abéché.

organizer.summary: The article does not identify an organizer of the funeral gathering.

participants_original.summary: HRW/CTDDH describe thousands attending the burial; a witness said signs stated they came in peace.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Reported attendance is thousands; whether the group was mobilized to protest rather than attend a funeral is unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The source reports peaceful signs but does not establish that all attendees refrained from violence; no explicit assessment of attendee violence is provided.

state_response.killings.summary: HRW/CTDDH report ten people killed during the Jan 25 cemetery shooting.

state_response.shootings.summary: HRW/CTDDH report soldiers indiscriminately firing live rounds at people attending the burial.

demands.summary: The source reports peaceful signs but does not identify a distinct demand made by the burial crowd.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The report documents shooting at funeral attendees but does not state that this was an attempt to disperse the gathering.

notes: Kept distinct from the Jan 24 march. The source establishes a large funeral gathering, peaceful signs, and a deadly state shooting, but does not establish an independent protest action or an explicit state/policy demand by the funeral attendees. Retain for coordinator review rather than merging or treating the funeral alone as a protest.
open_questions: Did attendees make an explicit demand or undertake a protest action in addition to the burial?
Were signs/chanting directed at authorities or only describing intent to remain peaceful?
Any independent contemporary account describes the event as a demonstration?

corrections.rationale: The source documents the funeral gathering and shooting on Jan 25 only; a report describing one day does not establish the physical end. End precision reset to unknown.
Peaceful signs indicate a stated intent, but the source does not explicitly assess whether any attendees engaged in violence. Absence of a violence report alone is not coded no_explicit.

title: Les Transformateurs opposition meeting at Idriss Mahamat Ouya stadium
organizer: Les Transformateurs, led by Succès Masra
participants_original: VOA Afrique describes a “marée humaine” in a stadium “full to bursting”; no count supplied.
threshold_50_evidence: The largest N’Djamena stadium was reported full to bursting, with a large crowd described as a human tide. This comfortably exceeds 50, though no numerical estimate is provided.

start_date.summary: VOA dates the meeting to Saturday, January 8, 2022.

end_date.summary: The report locates the meeting on Jan 8 but gives no physical ending date; end date remains unknown.

location.summary: The meeting was held in Idriss Mahamat Ouya stadium in N’Djamena.

scope.summary: One local stadium meeting in N’Djamena.

organizer.summary: The article identifies Les Transformateurs president Succès Masra as the meeting leader.

demands.summary: Speakers called for a sincere, inclusive dialogue to set transition rules and free democratic elections.

participants_original.summary: VOA calls the crowd a “marée humaine” and says the stadium was full to bursting.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A packed large stadium is credibly well over 50; no numeric bounds are invented.

protester_violence.summary: This report does not explicitly establish whether participants used violence; code remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The administration authorized the planned venue at the last minute; no substantive demand was fulfilled and no leadership meeting or agreed formal discussion is reported, so accommodation remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The large police presence was described as professionally surrounding the rally; no dispersal attempt is reported, but absence is not established.

state_response.ignore.summary: The account does not establish that authorities ignored the demands.

state_response.killings.summary: No deaths are reported in this account.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shooting is reported in this account.

notes: Large opposition party meeting with explicit transition-process and election demands; keep the meeting separate from Les Transformateurs’ later planned Jan 29 rally, which was cancelled in the discovery record. Permit for the rally is not coded as policy concession. Inclusion as a protest-type political gathering remains subject to original codebook/coordinator review.
open_questions: Does the verified original codebook include large party political meetings of this kind as protest events?
Can a second independent contemporary account refine authorization chronology and turnout?

corrections.rationale: Last-minute permission to hold a rally is not fulfillment of a substantive demand, leadership meeting, or agreed formal discussion; the existing field evidence and notes do not establish accommodation. Corrected after coordinator read.

The source establishes that the meeting happened on Jan 8 but does not establish a physical end date; a one-day report is not by itself evidence that the action ended that day. End precision reset to unknown after coordinator read.

title: MNCT rally in support of the CMT and national dialogue
location: Stadium in N’Djamena; the stadium is not named in the report.
organizer: National Movement for Change in Chad (MNCT), led by Mohamed Ahmed Lazina
participants_original: AFP/SWI: “thousands” gathered in a N’Djamena stadium; stands full.
threshold_50_evidence: AFP/SWI reports thousands at a stadium with filled stands, comfortably above 50; no numeric bound is inferred.

start_date.summary: AFP dates the rally to Saturday, January 22.

end_date.summary: AFP describes a rally on Jan 22 but does not establish a physical ending date.

location.summary: AFP places the event in a N’Djamena stadium but does not name the venue.

organizer.summary: AFP identifies MNCT as convener and Mohamed Ahmed Lazina as its leader.

participants_original.summary: AFP says thousands gathered and the stadium stands were filled.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The report’s “thousands” description is well over 50; no number is derived.

demands.summary: Speakers urged opponents and rebels to join the government-led national dialogue; the story frames this as support for the authorities and does not establish a demand to the state.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not describe violence by participants; state remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: A serving minister addressed the supportive rally, but the article does not describe this as accommodation of an event demand.

state_response.ignore.summary: No information establishing whether the state ignored an event demand.

state_response.killings.summary: No deaths reported in this account.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shootings reported in this account.

notes: Supportive political gathering for the military transition and dialogue process, not automatically coded as protest. Keep distinct from any same-day MUR event until organizer and event boundaries are established. Source is AFP wire copy; derivative reports do not count as independent origins.
open_questions: Does a supportive rally without a state-directed grievance qualify under the verified original codebook?
Is this same event as other Jan 22 support-meeting coverage?
Was there a separately organized MUR gathering or a single broader rally?

corrections.rationale: The one-day report gives the rally date but does not establish a physical end; end precision reset to unknown.

title: Abena secondary-school student demonstration over return of mathematics teacher
location: Lycée d’Abena, commune of the 7th arrondissement, N’Djamena; nearby road not identified
participants_original: Ialtchad reports students from the lycée taking to the street and identifies first-year students in its account, but gives no attendance count.
threshold_50_evidence: The article confirms a student street action but supplies no crowd count or reliable estimate; it does not establish 50 participants. Eligibility remains pending_threshold.

start_date.summary: The Jan 28 article dates the student action to Wednesday Jan 26.

end_date.summary: The report dates the action but does not establish when the gathering physically ended; end remains unknown.

location.summary: Ialtchad places the school in the commune of N’Djamena’s 7th arrondissement; the road is not named.

organizer.summary: No organizer is identified; the article describes students responding to the absence of their mathematics teacher.

demands.summary: Students sought the return of their mathematics teacher, who was absent during a strike by state contract science teachers. The article does not establish that students directed a demand to the state or government policy; no original demand category is assigned.

participants_original.summary: The article reports students in the street and describes first-year pupils raising the issue, without reporting crowd size.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance count or reliable size estimate is provided; 50-person threshold remains unverified.

protester_violence.summary: The article attributes burning a commercial minibus to students but does not establish that the vehicle belonged to or was directed against the state. The local codebook defines this field as violence against the state, so the field remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The headmaster is quoted as attempting to resolve the dispute with pupils and releasing them before the road action. The timing and status of this school-level interaction do not establish accommodation in response to an eligible protest demand; code remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No state attempt to disperse the street gathering is reported.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not establish whether authorities ignored a demand directed to the state.

state_response.killings.summary: A pupil died after being run over while attempting to board a commercial minibus; the report does not describe a state-caused death.

notes: Occurrence and Jan 26 date are body-verified. Students sought return of their math teacher during an ongoing strike by state contract science teachers. The source reports road obstruction and a minibus burned by students; one pupil died in a transport accident while trying to board it. No crowd size is stated and the article does not establish a clear state-directed demand; do not treat the accidental death as a state killing. Coding correction: an earlier value of yes treated the reported minibus fire as protester violence without evidence of a state-owned or state-directed target; following the local codebook definition (violence against the state), the field is now unknown. The reported fire remains in the narrative. The pupil’s accidental death remains distinct from a state killing. Eligibility correction: both the 50-person threshold and a state-directed demand remain unverified, so the record is pending_evidence rather than only pending_threshold.
open_questions: What was the turnout, and can a credible source establish at least 50 participants?
Was the demand directed to a government or state policy authority rather than school administration?
Does the principal’s pre-action conversation count as a state accommodation response under the original rules?
When did the crowd action physically end?

title: Doba students’ class boycott over teacher shortages
location: Lycée Pascal Yoadoumndji and CEG Beraba, Doba; any separate gathering site is unestablished
participants_original: A contributor-reviewed source reports students at two schools boycotting classes from Jan 31 through Feb 2. It gives no student or crowd count.
threshold_50_evidence: No count or estimate is reported; the 50-person threshold is unverified. Enrollment and schools served are not attendance counts.

start_date.summary: Registered contributor /root/chad_transport_students_verification reports that the article dates the two-school class boycott from Jan 31 through Feb 2. This is the reported class-boycott onset only; the source does not establish the start date of a qualifying public gathering.

end_date.summary: The article is summarized as reporting class boycotts through Feb 2, but the contributor did not find a definitive physical gathering endpoint. This record describes the boycott strand only; no gathering end is assigned.

location.summary: The contributor identifies Lycée Pascal Yoadoumndji and CEG Beraba in Doba as the schools whose students boycotted classes; a separate gathering site is not established.

scope.summary: The reported student action involves two schools in Doba.

organizer.summary: The article identifies students at the two schools but no formal organizer.

demands.summary: The contributor reports a student demand for missing science, French and history teachers. The article separately describes a meeting with the national education delegate, but the date of that meeting/gathering is not established; no demand category is assigned pending the original coding procedure.

participants_original.summary: The contributor reports students at two named schools boycotting classes; no numerical count is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or estimate appears in the reported account; threshold is unverified.

protester_violence.summary: A separate Feb 2 strand describes projectiles against school buildings. The contributor reports that the target is not identified as state property; this later strand is not assigned to the January boycott and does not establish violence against the state.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The account describes an education-delegate meeting and promise of science teachers, but the date and relation to the Jan 31 boycott onset are not established. Do not code as a January accommodation without coordinator boundary review.

state_response.arrests.summary: The contributor reports unspecified arrests in the separate Feb 2 confrontation; not assigned to the Jan 31 boycott or January state response.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beating information is established for the Jan 31 class-boycott strand.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The contributor reports police tear gas in a separate Feb 2 confrontation; its relationship to the January boycott or any Jan gathering is not established.

state_response.ignore.summary: The source does not establish whether authorities ignored a demand during a January gathering.

state_response.killings.summary: No killing information is established for the January class-boycott strand.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shooting information is established for the January class-boycott strand.

notes: This draft preserves only the student class-boycott strand explicitly reported by registered contributor /root/chad_transport_students_verification; Jan 31 is the reported boycott onset, not an established qualifying public-gathering start; the contributor’s exact-URL fallback returned HTTP 200 with no redirect, and its saved body receipt hash is 5241ae3a7e2e4fd16cde69aeaced69f641f40356705ad8325bbd40a3603b4591. This writer has not read the full article body. The source reports the student action through Feb 2 but does not establish a qualifying crowd of 50, a separate public-gathering date, the precise official meeting date, or a physical gathering end. Do not use Jan 31 boycott onset as the date of a separate public gathering, and do not carry the Feb 2 confrontation’s tear gas/arrests back into January. S026 itself does not date its teacher strike; separate body-read S020/S021 articles report a contract science-teacher work stoppage launched Jan 3, but document no in-person assembly, location or turnout and do not establish a Doba student gathering date or participant count. Do not treat the teachers as participants in E007. The source prints the later date as Tuesday, though Feb 2, 2022 was Wednesday; retain the date and flag the weekday discrepancy for review.
open_questions: Does the reported class boycott itself fall within the original event unit without a separately dated public gathering?
Was there a qualifying public assembly, and when did it occur? Do not infer Jan 31 from the class-boycott start.
Can a credible source establish at least 50 participants in a qualifying January action?
When did the education-delegate meeting occur, and is it part of a January episode?
What is the physical end date, if a qualifying gathering occurred?
Does the February unit record the Feb 2 confrontation as a separate episode or continuation?
